study_design: Prospective matched nested case-control study within the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study
reason: The abstract evaluates prostate cancer risk using prediagnostic serum measurements but does not report an aggressive, advanced, high-grade, metastatic, or lethal incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Serum DBP modified the association between serum 25(OH)D and prostate cancer, with higher risk for elevated 25(OH)D levels observed primarily among men having DBP concentrations above the median (OR = 1.81, 95% CI: 1.18-2.79 for highest vs. lowest quintile, p-trend = 0.001) compared to those with DBP below the median (OR = 1.22, 95% CI: 0.81-1.84, p-trend 0.97; p-interaction = 0.04).
estimate_classifications.reason: This estimate concerns overall prostate cancer risk, with no aggressive disease definition.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: We recently reported a significant positive association between 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], the accepted biomarker of vitamin D status, and prostate cancer risk.
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied full-text estimate is identified as incident prostate cancer, and the abstract supports only a general prostate cancer risk endpoint.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
